body.statement: Fix \(\Gamma=4\), \(h>0\), and \(0<\alpha<1/2\). At \(\theta_0\), \(C_{P_{\theta_0}}(0)=9/25\), whereas at \(\theta_{n,h}\), \(C_{P_{\theta_{n,h}}}(0)=+\infty\) for every sufficiently large \(n\), and the total variation distance between \(P_{\theta_0}^{\otimes n}\) and \(P_{\theta_{n,h}}^{\otimes n}\) tends to zero. Consequently, any random set \(\mathcal C_n\) satisfying \(P_{\vartheta}^{\otimes n}\{C_{P_{\vartheta}}(0)\in\mathcal C_n\}\geq1-\alpha\) for both \(\vartheta\in\{\theta_0,\theta_{n,h}\}\) obeys \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}P_{\theta_0}^{\otimes n}\{\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal C_n)=+\infty\}\geq1-2\alpha\).
body.justification: The contiguous two-point argument quantifies why no uniformly honest finite-width interval can cross the finite-to-infinite null-feasibility boundary.
body.gap: Standard directional-bootstrap theory presumes a finite local parameter; it does not provide this extended-real boundary impossibility result for a sensitivity frontier.
body.consumer: An analyst is told when an infinite upper endpoint is statistically unavoidable rather than a numerical failure of the profile algorithm.
